author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Tune touchscreen opacity and size for readability
summary: Tune touch controls against bright and dark game scenes, changing opacity, size, and position separately so inputs remain readable without covering essential PS2 content.
heroAlt: A person playing a game on a smartphone while both thumbs cover parts of the screen, illustrating real touch-control visibility and reach

sourceLabels.android-controller-events: Android button, axis, and device event guidance

blocks.text: Tune the overlay against two opposite scenes
Balance readable PS2 video with controls that remain visible, reachable, and distinguishable under the thumbs.
Reducing opacity until a screenshot looks clean can make live controls vanish during fast or high-contrast gameplay.

items: Default overlay screenshot saved in the normal orientation.
Bright and dark repeatable game scenes available.
Essential HUD zones and gesture insets identified.

blocks.text: Adjust one visual property per pass

items: 1. Open the bright scene and mark controls that blend into highlights.
2. Open the dark scene and mark controls that lose their outlines.
3. Raise or lower opacity in one small step without resizing.
4. Test every button under a resting thumb rather than only by sight.
5. Resize only targets that are missed or overlap neighboring controls.
6. Move controls away from essential HUD elements and system gesture edges.
7. Play an action sequence that combines movement, camera, and two buttons.
8. Save the layout with orientation and device class in its name.

blocks.text: Opacity solves visual obstruction, size solves targeting accuracy, and position solves conflicts with game content; changing all three together hides the responsible variable.
Accept readable controls without visual sacrifice
Every required touch target remains legible and reachable while important HUD and action areas stay visible in both bright and dark scenes.

items: All required controls remain visible in bright and dark scenes.
Thumb targeting does not trigger adjacent buttons.
Critical game HUD information remains readable during active input.
Buttons disappear only on highlights: strengthen outline or opacity rather than enlarging all controls.
Adjacent buttons misfire: increase separation before global scaling.
The HUD is covered: reposition the conflicting group for this game.
System gestures interrupt play: respect the safe gesture region.

blocks.text: Reload the captured default overlay and delete only the readability experiment.
A readable screenshot is not a complete touch test
Thumbs cover pixels, pressure changes grip, and motion shifts reach; evaluate the layout during continuous play rather than from an untouched screen alone.
